info.name: Track. Enterprise API Collection
info.description:
API collection for the Track Multi-User Enterprise Task Tracker, backed by SQLite.

**Auth model**: cookie-based sessions (`session_token`, httpOnly). Postman's built-in cookie jar handles this automatically once you run **Login** — no manual header wiring needed. There is no Bearer/API-key auth in this API.

**Roles**: every user is either a regular user or an admin (`isAdmin`). "Manager" and "employee" are not fixed roles — they're derived from rows in the `manager_employee` table, so any user can be a manager of some people and a report of others. Endpoints under **Admin (User & Hierarchy)** require `isAdmin = true` on the calling session (403 otherwise); endpoints under **Team & Hierarchy** just need an authenticated session (no admin flag), since they only ever return data scoped to the caller; all other endpoints likewise just require an authenticated session (401 otherwise).

**Two known scoping gaps, documented on their requests rather than hidden**: `GET /api/reports/manager` (Team & Hierarchy) aggregates a report's task/time totals company-wide instead of scoping to what the calling manager can actually see; `POST /api/projects/:id/members` (Projects) lets an owner add any active company user, not just their own direct reports. Neither crashes anything — see each request's description for the specifics.

**Self-signup is locked down**: `POST /api/auth/signup` only succeeds while the system has zero users (it creates the first account as admin). After that it always returns 403 — new accounts must be created via **Provision User (Admin)**.

**Suggested run order** (this collection is wired for it via test scripts that auto-populate collection variables like `{{projectId}}`, `{{taskId}}`, `{{managerUserId}}`, `{{employeeUserId}}`, `{{templateId}}` — no manual copy-pasting of IDs required):
1. Authentication → Sign Up (only if the DB is empty) → Login
2. Admin → provision a manager + an employee, link them
3. Team & Hierarchy → confirm the link (Get My Direct Reports / Get My Managers), try the rollups
4. Projects → create a project (as the logged-in admin/manager)
5. Tasks → create/update/bulk-update a task, assigning it to the employee
6. Templates → create a template, spin up a project from it

Within each folder, non-destructive requests are ordered first; **Delete**/**Unassign** requests are last and destructive — run them only once you're done exploring that folder.

item.name: Authentication

exec: console.log('System already has users — self-signup is disabled by design. Use Login instead.');

request.description:
Registers a new account **only if the `users` table is currently empty** — that account is automatically flagged `isAdmin = true`. Once any user exists, this always returns `403 {"error":"Self-signup is disabled. New user accounts must be provisioned by an administrator."}`. There is no way to re-enable open signup short of an empty database; use **Provision User (Admin)** for every account after the first.

**Responses**
- `201` — `{ "message": "System administrator registered successfully!" }`
- `400` — missing `username`/`password`, or username already taken
- `403` — system already initialized (expected on any run after the first)

response.name: 403 Forbidden — signup already disabled

exec: pm.test('Login succeeded and returned a user profile', function () {

request.description:
Verifies credentials, writes a hashed session row to SQLite (7-day expiry), and sets an `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` `session_token` cookie. Postman's cookie jar stores this automatically for `{{baseUrl}}` — every subsequent request in this collection reuses it without any manual setup.

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "message": "Login successful!", "user": { "id", "username", "email", "displayName", "jobTitle", "isAdmin" } }`
- `400` — missing `username`/`password`
- `401` — invalid username or password

Returns the profile bound to the active session cookie. Useful as a quick "am I still logged in / am I admin" check before running admin-only requests.

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "user": { "id", "username", "email", "displayName", "jobTitle", "isAdmin" } }`
- `401` — no session cookie, or session missing/expired in the database

Deletes the session row from SQLite and clears the `session_token` cookie. Idempotent — safe to call even with no active session.

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "message": "Logged out successfully." }` (always, even if there was nothing to log out of)

item.description: Session lifecycle: bootstrap the first admin, sign in, inspect the current session, sign out. Run **Login** before anything else in this collection — every other folder depends on its cookie.

item.name: Admin (User & Hierarchy)

request.description:
Lists every user in the org with their derived `managerIds` (who they report to) and `employeeIds` (who reports to them) — computed from the `manager_employee` table, not stored on the user row. **Admin only.**

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, username, email, displayName, jobTitle, isAdmin, isActive, createdAt, managerIds: [], employeeIds: [] }`
- `401` — not logged in
- `403` — logged in but not an admin

Creates a user account directly — this is the only supported way to add people once the system has been bootstrapped (self-signup is disabled). Sets `managerUserId` from the response for later requests. "Manager" isn't a role flag here; this account becomes a manager the moment someone reports to it (see **Assign Manager**). **Admin only.**

**Responses**
- `201` — `{ "message": "User provisioned successfully.", "userId" }`
- `400` — missing `username`/`password`, or username already taken
- `403` — caller is not an admin

Same endpoint as **Provision Manager Account** — creates the employee standalone (no manager yet) so the next request can demonstrate **Assign Manager** explicitly. You could equally pass `managerIds: ["{{managerUserId}}"]` here to link at creation time; both paths run the same cycle-detection check. **Admin only.**

Partially updates a user's profile — every field is optional and only supplied fields are changed (`COALESCE` under the hood). **Important**: if you include `managerIds` in the body, it **fully replaces** that user's manager set (existing links not in the list are deleted first) — omit it entirely to leave manager relationships untouched, as this example does. Setting `isActive: false` immediately blocks that user from authenticating (checked in the login and session-lookup queries). **Admin only.**

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "message": "User updated successfully." }`
- `404` — user ID not found
- `403` — caller is not an admin

exec: pm.test('Manager link created (or already existed)', function () {

request.description:
Links `managerId` as a manager of `employeeId`. An employee can have multiple managers — this just adds another row, it never replaces existing links. A breadth-first cycle check walks the existing hierarchy before inserting, so a manager can never end up (directly or transitively) reporting to their own report. Re-running this with the same pair is a harmless no-op (`INSERT OR IGNORE`). **Admin only.**

**Responses**
- `201` — `{ "message": "Manager assigned successfully." }`
- `400` — missing `managerId`/`employeeId`, or the pair would create a cycle
- `403` — caller is not an admin

response.name: 400 Bad Request — would create a hierarchy loop

request.description:
Removes one manager-employee link. Idempotent — returns `200` even if the pair wasn't linked. **Destructive to the demo hierarchy — run this last**, since later requests in the Tasks folder rely on the manager/employee link to demonstrate assignee validation. **Admin only.**

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "message": "Manager unassigned successfully." }` (always)
- `403` — caller is not an admin

item.description: Admin-only endpoints (403 for any non-admin session) for provisioning accounts and shaping the manager/employee hierarchy. Run **Provision Manager Account** and **Provision Employee Account** before **Assign Manager** — both earlier requests auto-populate `{{managerUserId}}`/`{{employeeUserId}}` via their test scripts.

item.name: Team & Hierarchy

request.description:
Returns the people who report **directly** to the logged-in user, derived live from `manager_employee` (there's no stored "is a manager" flag — you're a manager purely because this list is non-empty). Used by the frontend to compute `isManager`.

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, username, email, displayName, jobTitle, isAdmin }` (empty array if you manage no one)

Returns everyone who directly manages the logged-in user. Can be more than one — an employee having multiple managers is a supported case, not an edge case.

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, username, email, displayName, jobTitle, isAdmin }` (empty array if you have no manager)

Like **Get My Direct Reports**, but walks the full hierarchy with a `WITH RECURSIVE` query — direct reports, their reports, and so on. Backs the **Team Directory** frontend view. De-duplicated even if someone is reachable through more than one management chain.

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, username, email, displayName, jobTitle, isAdmin }`

query.description: Optional. Include to also pull in this project's members as candidates.

request.description:
Populates the assignee dropdown shown in the task create/edit modal: always includes yourself and your direct reports; if `projectId` is given, also includes that project's members (de-duplicated). This is deliberately the same rule set `isValidAssignee` enforces server-side on task create/update, so the dropdown never offers a choice the backend would reject.

Omit `projectId` (or drop the query string entirely) to get just yourself + direct reports, useful outside a project context.

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, username, email, displayName, jobTitle, isAdmin }`
- `404` — a `projectId` was given but you don't own it and aren't a member (same check task creation uses)

response.name: 404 Not Found — no access to that project

request.description:
Skip-level performance rollup across every direct and indirect report (via `getRecursiveReports`) — a summary block plus one stats entry per report (task counts by status, completion rate, overdue count, total time logged, and that report's own list of managers).

**⚠️ Known scoping gap (documented, not fixed as of this API version)**: per-report stats are computed with `SELECT ... FROM tasks WHERE assignee_id = ?` and are **not** filtered by project visibility — they include every task ever assigned to that person company-wide, even ones created by a completely unrelated manager in a project you have no access to. Verified: a manager whose only relationship to an employee is via `manager_employee` will see that employee's *combined* task/time totals from every manager who has ever assigned them anything, not just their own. Contrast with **Get Project Time Rollup** below, which *is* correctly scoped to one project's visibility. Treat the numbers here as "this person's total workload across the company," not "work I personally assigned or can see."

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ summary: { totalReports, teamTotalTasks, teamCompletedTasks, teamCompletionRate, teamOverdueTasks, teamTotalTimeLogged }, reports: [{ user, managers: [...], stats: { totalTasks, completedTasks, inProgressTasks, todoTasks, overdueTasks, completionRate, totalTimeLogged } }] }` (empty `reports` array if you manage no one)

Lists every active user in the company (id, username, displayName, jobTitle, email) — used to populate the "add teammate to project" candidate picker. **Any authenticated user can call this**, not just admins or managers; there's no scoping to the caller's own reports or existing projects. Reasonable for an internal tool's people-picker, but worth confirming that company-wide visibility (including everyone's email) is the intended scope.

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, username, displayName, jobTitle, email }`

item.description: Read-only endpoints exposing the manager/employee hierarchy and cross-user directory data — everything here just requires an authenticated session (no admin flag needed, unlike the **Admin** folder). Run after **Assign Manager** so the recursive/rollup endpoints have real hierarchy data to show.

item.name: Projects

request.description:
Returns every project the current user can see: projects they own, plus projects where they appear in `project_members`. Each project includes its full `tasks` array and a `members` array. **Note**: the `members` entries come straight from the database and use snake_case field names (`display_name`, `job_title`, `joined_at`), unlike every other camelCase response in this API — that's a real quirk of the current implementation, not a typo in this doc.

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, name, description, url, github, ownerId, createdAt, members: [{ id, username, display_name, job_title, joined_at }], tasks: [...] }`
- `401` — not logged in

Creates a project owned by the logged-in user and automatically adds them as a `project_members` row (so they show up as a member on subsequent `GET`s). Sets `{{projectId}}` from the response for use in the Tasks and later Projects requests. **Quirk to note**: the creation response itself always reports `"members": []` even though the owner membership row was just inserted — a follow-up `GET /api/projects` will correctly show it. Only `name` is required.

**Responses**
- `201` — the new project (see shape above; `tasks` and `members` empty in this response)
- `400` — missing `name`

Updates project metadata. **Owner only** — a project member who isn't the owner gets `403`, even though members can freely add/edit tasks inside the project (see Tasks folder).

**Responses**
- `200` — the updated project, with live `tasks`/`members` arrays
- `400` — missing `name`
- `403` — logged-in user is a member but not the owner
- `404` — project doesn't exist

response.name: 403 Forbidden — not the owner

request.description:
Adds an active user as a member of the project — from then on they get full board visibility (every task, not just ones assigned to them) per the collaborative-project design. **Owner only.**

**⚠️ No hierarchy check**: unlike task-assignment (`isValidAssignee`, which restricts to self/member/direct-report), this endpoint lets an owner add **any** active user in the company, not just their own direct reports — despite "manager adds their own report" being the original design intent. Confirmed: an owner with zero management relationship to a user can still add them. Worth knowing if you're relying on org-hierarchy as an access boundary.

**Responses**
- `201` — `{ message, members: [{ id, username, displayName, jobTitle, email, joinedAt }] }` (full updated member list)
- `400` — missing `userId`
- `403` — caller is not the project owner
- `404` — project doesn't exist, or `userId` doesn't match an active user

response.name: 403 Forbidden — not the owner

request.description:
Revokes a member's access to the project (they immediately lose the full-board visibility membership granted). **Owner only**, and the owner is explicitly protected from removing themselves — there's no way to leave your own project via this endpoint (delete the project instead if that's the goal).

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ message, members: [...] }` (full updated member list, always returned even if the given `userId` wasn't a member)
- `400` — attempted to remove the project owner
- `403` — caller is not the project owner
- `404` — project doesn't exist

response.name: 400 Bad Request — cannot remove the owner

request.description:
Aggregates logged time for this **one project only** — correctly scoped by `WHERE project_id = ?` throughout (contrast with **Get Manager Performance Rollup** in the Team & Hierarchy folder, which is not project-scoped). Requires project ownership or membership.

Returns four views of the same underlying `time_sessions`/`tasks` data:
- `totalProjectTimeSeconds` — sum of `time_logged` across every task in the project
- `memberRollup` — total time + task count per assignee, sorted highest first
- `taskRollup` — top 20 tasks by time logged (only tasks with `time_logged > 0`)
- `sessions` — the 50 most recent individual timer sessions, newest first

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ projectId, projectName, totalProjectTimeSeconds, memberRollup: [...], taskRollup: [...], sessions: [...] }`
- `404` — project doesn't exist, or caller isn't the owner/a member

Deletes the project and cascades to every task, task assignment, time session, and membership row underneath it (both via SQLite `ON DELETE CASCADE` and explicit cleanup queries as a belt-and-suspenders measure). **Owner only** — an outsider or non-owner member gets `404`, and this action cannot be undone. **Run this last** — Tasks, Templates, and the member/time-rollup requests above all reuse `{{projectId}}`.

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "message": "Project deleted successfully." }`
- `404` — project doesn't exist, or caller isn't the owner

item.description: Project CRUD, scoped to whatever the logged-in user owns or is a member of, plus owner-only membership management and a project-scoped time-tracking rollup. Editing/deleting metadata and managing members is owner-only; adding tasks is open to any project member (see Tasks folder).

item.name: Tasks

body.raw:
{
    "title": "Implement User Authentication",
    "description": "Create login and signup endpoints with SQLite storage.",
    "status": "todo",
    "priority": "high",
    "scheduleDate": "2026-09-01T09:00",
    "deadline": "2026-09-15T17:00",
    "reminder": true,
    "urgent": true,
    "important": true,
    "assigneeId": "{{employeeUserId}}",
    "subtasks": [
        { "id": "s1", "text": "Setup SQLite tables", "completed": true },
        { "id": "s2", "text": "Add session cookies", "completed": true }
    ],
    "timeLogged": 0,
    "timeSessions": [],
    "timerStarted": null,
    "pomodoroSessions": []
}

request.description:
Creates a task in the project. Requires the caller to own the project or be a member. `assigneeId` is optional — omit it to self-assign — but if provided, it's validated server-side: it must be an active user who is either the caller themself, a member of this project, or a **direct** report of the caller. This example demonstrates the manager→direct-report case, so **Assign Manager** must have run first for it to pass.

**Responses**
- `201` — the new task, `assigneeId`/`createdById` reflecting who it's for and who made it
- `400` — missing `title`, or `assigneeId` fails the checks above
- `404` — project doesn't exist or caller has no access to it

response.name: 400 Bad Request — invalid assignee

body.raw:
{
    "title": "Implement User Authentication",
    "description": "Create login and signup endpoints with SQLite storage.",
    "status": "done",
    "priority": "high",
    "scheduleDate": "2026-09-01T09:00",
    "deadline": "2026-09-15T17:00",
    "reminder": true,
    "urgent": true,
    "important": true,
    "timeLogged": 3600,
    "timeSessions": [
        { "id": "sess1", "startTime": "2026-09-01T09:00:00Z", "endTime": "2026-09-01T10:00:00Z", "duration": 3600 }
    ]
}

request.description:
Full update of a task's fields. Requires project ownership/membership (checked before the task lookup). Setting `status` to `"done"` stamps `completedAt`; moving it back off `"done"` clears it. `timeSessions` entries are upserted into the normalized `time_sessions` table (used for the time-tracking rollups) in addition to updating the task's own `timeLogged` cache. Re-supplying `assigneeId` with a *different* value re-runs the same validation as task creation; leaving it unchanged skips re-validation.

**Responses**
- `200` — the updated task
- `400` — missing `title`, or a changed `assigneeId` fails validation
- `404` — project not found/unauthorized, or task doesn't exist in this project

One endpoint, three `action` values — pick one per call by editing the body:
- `"action": "status", "value": "todo" | "in-progress" | "done"` — bulk status change (stamps/clears `completedAt` per task, same as a single update)
- `"action": "priority", "value": "low" | "medium" | "high"` — bulk priority change
- `"action": "delete"` (`value` ignored) — bulk permanent delete

See the saved example responses on this request for the priority and delete variants. Requires project ownership/membership; `taskIds` outside the given `projectId` are silently skipped rather than erroring.

**Responses**
- `200` — the project's full remaining task list after the operation
- `400` — empty/missing `taskIds`, or missing `action`
- `404` — project not found or caller has no access to it

response.name: 404 Not Found — no access to project

request.description:
Permanently deletes a single task (and its `time_sessions` rows, via cascade). Requires project ownership/membership. **Run this last** in the folder — it consumes `{{taskId}}`.

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "message": "Task deleted successfully." }`
- `404` — project not found/unauthorized, or task doesn't exist

item.description: Task CRUD scoped to project access — every request here now requires the caller to own the project or be a member of it (previously only task *creation* enforced this; `PUT`/`DELETE`/bulk are equally protected). Chained via `{{projectId}}`/`{{taskId}}` from the Projects folder.

item.name: Templates

request.description:
Lists the current user's own saved templates (owner-scoped, not shared across users). Does **not** include the two built-in templates (`onboarding`, `sprint`) — those exist only as hardcoded fallbacks inside **Spin Up Project from Template** and aren't listed anywhere.

**Responses**
- `200` — array of `{ id, name, description, category, tasks: [...], createdAt }`

Saves a reusable task-list snapshot owned by the caller. Only `title`, `description`, `priority`, `urgent`, `important`, and `subtasks` are kept per task — any other fields on the input `tasks` are dropped. Sets `{{templateId}}` for use in **Spin Up Project from Template**.

**Responses**
- `201` — the created template
- `400` — missing `name`

Creates a brand-new project (caller becomes owner + member) and instantiates every task from the template. `:templateId` accepts either a real template UUID you own (as used here via `{{templateId}}`) **or** one of two hardcoded string IDs that need no prior setup: `onboarding` (3-task client-onboarding flow) or `sprint` (4-task agile sprint plan). `projectName`/`projectDescription` override the template's own name/description if provided.

**Responses**
- `201` — the new project with its instantiated `tasks`
- `404` — `:templateId` is neither one of your own template IDs nor `onboarding`/`sprint`

Permanently deletes a template you own. Silently succeeds even if the ID doesn't exist or belongs to someone else — the query is scoped by `owner_id` but the endpoint doesn't distinguish "not found" from "not yours" in its response. **Run this last** in the folder.

**Responses**
- `200` — `{ "message": "Template deleted." }` (always)

item.description: Reusable task-list templates, owner-scoped, plus the endpoint that turns a template into a live project.
